subject: english
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 3'** i.e.** 'About'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate word to fill in blank number 4 is **option 3: "about".**
 
• In this context, **"about"** is used to indicate an approximation.
 
• It's** often used** when you don't have an exact figure but want to give a general idea.
 
• The sentence is trying to give an approximate comparison of the size of the Bosavi woolly rat to a cat, hence **"about"** is the most suitable choice.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'According to the Integrated Taxonomic Information System (ITIS) there are more than 60 species of rat, which means they come in all sizes. They are typically 5 inches (12 centimeters), or longer, according to Encyclopedia Britannica. The largest species is the Bosavi woolly rat, which was discovered in 2009 in the rainforest of Papua New Guinea (and doesn't have a scientific name yet). It is **about **the size of a cat - 32.2 inches (82 cm) from nose to tail and (5)______ around 3.3 lbs. (1.5 kilograms), according to CNN.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other options do not fit as well in this context:
 
 
• **"A lot" **- This term is usually used to indicate a large amount or number of something, but it doesn't fit in this context because we're comparing sizes, not quantities.
 
• **"Of" **- This is a preposition that can show relationships between parts of a sentence, but it doesn't work in this context.
 
• **"Some"** - This term is typically used to refer to an unspecified amount or number, but it doesn't fit in this context because we're comparing sizes, not referring to an amount.
